grass_base_growth.caption: Lolium perenne, a growing leaf: the zone where cells divide is under 1 mm long; the zone where they go on lengthening is 31-36 mm (cv. Condesa; the two values in each pair are the two phosphorus treatments).

grass_tillering.caption: Tiller density in an established perennial ryegrass sward: 5,000 to 7,000 per square metre (AHDB).

grass_blade.caption: A few sizes on a ryegrass leaf: blade width 2-4 mm (DELTA), ligule 1-2 mm (DELTA, Minnesota Wildflowers), and a pollen grain 26-50 µm (PalDat) for comparison.

grass_stoma.caption: Stomata are 10 to 80 micrometres long across species (Wikipedia: Stoma); a ryegrass pollen grain is 26-50 µm (PalDat). Neither is a measurement of ryegrass stomata.

grass_c3_c4.caption: C4 photosynthesis: rare among plant species but common among grasses and responsible for about a quarter of land photosynthesis (Wikipedia, C4 carbon fixation).

grass_spikelet.caption: Sizes in a ryegrass spikelet from floras: lemma 4-8.5 mm, spikelet 7-15 mm (typical range), anther 2.9-3.4 mm (DELTA).

grass_pollen.caption: Pollen grain size: 26-50 µm (PalDat); the sub-pollen particles released in rain are about 60-200 nm (0.06-0.2 µm); a human hair is 50-100 µm (Skin card).

bars.label: Asthma + Lung UK: levels often highest from month 5 (mid-May)

grass_hay_fever.caption: Grass pollen season in Britain: it can start as early as May and generally peaks in June and July (Met Office); levels are often highest between mid-May and July (Asthma + Lung UK).
